process.title: Creating & Photographing Spore Prints
process.subtitle: From forest foraging to photography — documenting how spore prints are crafted and captured up close.

step1.title: 01. Mushroom Foraging
step1.text: Wild specimens are ethically harvested across local Lithuanian forests and towns without disturbing the underground mycelial networks.

step2.title: 02. Identification & Research
step2.text: Before creating a print, each specimen is documented and identified using the guide "Didžioji Lietuvos grybų knyga".

step3.title: 03. Cap Preparation
step3.text: Stems are carefully trimmed and caps are dried for the preparation of printing.

step4.title: 04. Spore Collection
step4.text: Caps are placed on heavy paper or carton and kept covered for 8–12 hours, allowing the mushroom to naturally deposit its spores.

step5.title: 05. Macro Documentation
step5.text: Using a macro setup, I capture high-detail photography of the final spore compositions and fine surface textures.

a3_01.title: WIND DIRECTIONS
a3_01.desc: Spore prints of three fungi species on heavy carton paper.
a3_01.curatorNote:
Foraged on a damp afternoon in July 2026 around the streams of Verkių Regional Park.

This composition reveals the natural geometry and movement trajectory created as wild spores drift and deposit onto paper.

a3_02.title: DUNES OF DOUBT
a3_02.desc: Spore prints of four fungi species on heavy carton paper.
a3_02.curatorNote:
Foraged on a sunny afternoon in mid-July 2026 in Bukiškis town.

Each specimen left a distinct, unrepeatable deposit, showcasing the individual spore pigments and radial forms of wild fungi.
